dispositions.method: The automatic families first printed in 1805 that reach 4 or more papers, long-running ones included (story_items.py --long-running), were split into single printed items (items.json: 99 items in 7 or more papers by the finder's count, 15 in 9). Because some documents first printed in late 1804 reach the 1805 pages (the Chase impeachment, the acts of the session, Preble's letter), the script was also run with year 1804 over the 1805 pages (items_from_1804.json). The 1805 pages are those the base release dates to 1805 (year_search_pages.py --printed-dates), which adds the Kentucky Gazette issue of 28 May 1805 that the collection files under 1807. Two AI readers each read the items of half the year and proposed stories; their proposals were merged and checked here, and each item's printings were looked for with phrase searches over all 3,811 pages in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns.json, phrase_hits.json; keys that start 'candidate:' are items not admitted). Papers with pages in a story's weeks but no printing were searched with loose keywords; the scan pages whose RevX text is filed under another page were read in the CA transcription. Every admitted printing was then checked against its page scan (SCAN_PROTOCOL.md, scan_points.json).
dispositions.selection_rule: As for 1776, 1807 and 1808: every single item printed in 9 or more newspapers was admitted, except digests of unrelated paragraphs; items in 7 or 8 papers were chosen to cover the months and the main kinds of news. Every story alike (the owner's rule of 11 November 2026): no item was left out for its subject. Stories are counted item by item; where one publication holds several documents, or several documents belong to one affair, each is its own group under a parent story. A sub-story may have fewer than 7 papers when its parent reaches 7. The Portland Gazette's three titles of 1805 (Jenks' Portland Gazette, Portland Gazette, Portland Gazette and Maine Advertiser) count as one newspaper; no story's count depends on two of them.

counted_item_by_item.The declaration of Chase's acquittal: Quoted in four differently worded accounts of the court: the National Intelligencer's report with the votes (NI, EN, VA: 'Hence it appears that there is not a constitutional majority'), a shorter account with the senators' names (ADA, NG, BJ, RIR, OP: 'there not being a constitutional majority on any one article'), and NHG's own. Counted together as the declaration (role quoted_document), as 1807 counted the Burr verdict; split by wording, the largest form is in 5 papers.
counted_item_by_item.Chase's answer: A long document printed in parts; each paper counted once by its opening. ADA printed it from its beginning twice (16 and 20 February).
counted_item_by_item.The London paragraph on detaining Americ: Printed in two wordings, of 7 August ('we understand', 'not the produce') and 8 August ('it is said', 'not the property'): one paragraph with printed differences.
counted_item_by_item.The Privy Council's minute of 3 August: Published by three British consuls in three notices (Philadelphia, Virginia, New York) around the same quoted resolution; counted together as the minute.
counted_item_by_item.Barron's letter to Eaton: The official extract dated Malta, 22 March, and the letter with 'Dear Sir' dated 20 March (HUS, PGz): the same letter with a printed difference in the date.
counted_item_by_item.Napoleon's speech to the Senate: The Norfolk Gazette prints another translation; counted with the others (8 papers without it).
counted_item_by_item.The Salem Register report: The Portland Gazette of 2 September prints its own paragraph on the brig's arrival and then the Register's report; only the Register's report is the printing.
counted_item_by_item.The Paris article of 31 August: The Rhode-Island Republican prints its first part on 2 November and the rest on 14 November; counted once, by its opening.
